subject: Urgent: 45m maintenance window — compatibility hotpatch (inference runtime)
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acme.com>, Agnieszka Kowalska <agnieszka@bigcloud.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 2 Apr 2028 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Urgent: 45m maintenance window — compatibility hotpatch (inference runtime)

Jordan / Agnieszka — quick heads up from Redwood Ops: we discovered an interaction between a recent GPU driver update and our runtime's model KV cache path that increases tail latency and can cause intermittent 503s for long streaming sessions on certain model+hardware combinations (primarily in us-west).

We are scheduling an immediate hotpatch to address a kernel/driver compatibility path in the runtime. Planned window: 09:40–10:25 PT (approx 45 minutes). We will apply the hotpatch to a canary pool first, validate, then roll to the full us-west pool. Expected customer impact: short API errors (503) and connection resets for a subset of streaming/generation requests while a small subset of instances restart — we expect typical request latency to resume within the window.

What we recommend customers do now:
- Pause any non-essential long-running streams during the window.
- If you have active demos, schedule them after 11:00 PT or switch to the fallback model variant (see note below).
- Implement exponential backoff + retry (2–3 retries) for streaming attach/fetch calls during the window.

Mitigation available immediately: we will provision a fallback route to a quantized model variant (slightly lower throughput per request but avoids the affected kernel path). If you want us to opt your account into the fallback during the window, reply with APPROVE and we’ll flip it for Acme Corp.

Attachments: hotpatch_release_notes_v1.2.pdf (summary + risk), rollback_script.sh (ops), post_change_log.txt (ops).

I’ll post live updates to this thread and to the support ticket INC-2028-1129. Apologies for the short notice — we prioritized safety and minimizing a wider outage.

— Priyom
Priyom Das
Senior Technical Account Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acme.com>

Date: Tue, 2 Apr 2028 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Urgent: 45m maintenance window — compatibility hotpatch (inference runtime)

Thanks for the quick flag, Priyom. We have a product demo scheduled for 10:30 PT for a prospect — can you confirm whether switching Acme to the fallback variant will guarantee no connection resets for the demo? Also, what is the ETA for a postmortem and whether this will affect our SLA credit?

If fallback is safe, please go ahead (APPROVE). If not, we need a hard no-change during our demo window.

— Jordan

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Ops Team <ops@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 2 Apr 2028 09:30:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Urgent: 45m maintenance window — canary plan + rollback

Planned sequence (ops plan):
1) 09:40 — apply hotpatch to 2 canary hosts in us-west-1 (10% of traffic) and run smoke tests (latency, 100 streamed requests, KV cache hitrate).
2) 09:55 — if canary OK, rollout to remaining us-west pool in 3 waves (10m between waves).
3) 10:25 — expected completion; monitor 30m for regressions.

Fallback path: opt Acme into "quant-fallback-v2" (no kernel path used) — that avoids restarts; perf delta ~5–10% throughput per long request, quality identical for our use-case. Priyom, if Jordan approves we will flip routing at 09:38 to ensure connections bind to fallback before patch.

Rollback: we will use rollback_script.sh in the attachment to revert the patch and reimage affected instances if we see >1% 5xx rate sustained for 5 minutes.

Escalation contacts: Stephanie Nguyen (oncall infra lead) — 415-555-0199; Marcus Lin (SRE lead) available if needed.

Marissa
Marissa Cole
Director, Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 2 Apr 2028 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Completed — hotpatch applied & Acme routed to fallback for demo

Jordan — short update: we applied the hotpatch to canaries at 09:40, validated, and completed the rollout by 10:22 PT. Per your APPROVE, Acme was routed to quant-fallback-v2 at 09:38 and your demo at 10:30 did not see the connection resets we were observing on the primary path.

What happened: a driver edge-case triggered a racing path inside our KV cache eviction when sequence-lengths exceeded ~4k tokens on the affected hardware. The hotpatch removes the problematic kernel call and adds a safety check; full postmortem + remediation timeline will be posted to the runbook link (https://redwood.app/runbooks/compat-hotpatch-2028-04-02) and linked into INC-2028-1129.

Next steps we committed to Acme:
- Formal postmortem within 72 hours with root cause and permanent mitigation timeline.
- SLA review and credit assessment; our support team will follow up and apply credits if the incident meets SLA criteria.
- Offer for a short standing call this week to review any anomalies from your side.

Appreciate the quick coordination — let us know if you want us to keep Acme on the fallback for an additional 24 hours while we finish the postmortem.

— Priyom
